title: Surf From Across the World
question: What decides how big a wind wave gets, and how far it can go?
hook: Waves raised by heavy winds south of Tasmania can cross the Pacific and give surfers in southern California good waves.
idea: Wind speed, duration, fetch and depth limit how big wind waves grow, and once they leave the wind they can travel thousands of kilometres as swells.

beats.prompt: The same wind blows for the same time over two lakes of equal depth. One stretches 2 km in the wind's direction, the other 200 km. Which gets bigger waves?

choices.label: The 200 km lake, because of its longer fetch
The 2 km lake, because waves bounce back and stack up
choices.feedback: Fetch, the distance the wind blows over the water, is one of the limits on wave size, so a short stretch holds waves back.

choices.label: Both the same, since only wind speed matters
choices.feedback: Wind speed matters, but so do duration, fetch and depth.

beats.explain: Wave size is limited by fetch as well as wind speed, duration and depth, so the longer stretch of water lets bigger waves build.

beats.prompt: Sort each wave by the force that lets it travel
beats.explain: Small ripples, or capillary waves, are held by surface tension, while larger sea waves are driven mainly by gravity.

beats.prompt: Match each term to what it means
pairs: Distance the wind blows over the water
Waves still driven by the local wind
Waves that have left the wind's area
Average of the highest third of waves
beats.explain: These terms describe where waves come from, whether the wind still drives them, and how their height is reported.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: Wind blowing over water passes kinetic energy to the surface.
Waves can only gain energy while the wind outruns their crests.
Eventually the sea becomes fully developed for that wind.
So more of the same wind keeps making the waves taller forever.
beats.explain: A fully developed sea is the most that wind can build; further exposure only loses energy as wave tops break into whitecaps.
